issues.description: The problem statement gives contradictory guidance about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one part describes a final (instance) stock that should be initialized in the constructor, while a later explicit note mandates that the stock attribute must be static (shared across all instances). This also conflicts with the instruction to initialize it in the constructor, which implies an instance field. This ambiguity can confuse students about whether stock should be an instance-level final field initialized in the constructor or a static field initialized at class level.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement: explicitly state whether 'stock' is a shared static field or an instance-level final field. If the intent is a shared stock (as later notes and the reference solution implement), update the earlier description to say 'a static final Stock stock (shared across all saloons)' and remove the instruction to initialize it in the constructor (instead show static initialization). If the intent is an instance field, remove the requirement that stock and related methods be static. Ensure the UML and all textual instructions consistently reflect the same choice.
